key_insight: A hybrid silicon nanocone-plus-nanohole architecture improves light trapping by reducing front reflection and boosting internal scattering, enabling higher current and efficiency in thin-film solar cells.
engineering_relevance: This design offers a practical optical-structuring strategy for raising thin-film silicon photovoltaic performance while maintaining strong thermal robustness under operating conditions.
method: Front-surface silicon nanocones create a gradual refractive-index transition to suppress reflection.
Embedded air-filled nanoholes enhance absorption through multiple scattering and internal reflection.
FDTD-based optical optimization was coupled with electrical and opto-electro-thermal device simulations.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% FF, and 24.42% efficiency, with 95.21% efficiency retention up to 45 °C.
watch_item: The proposed gains depend on precise nanoscale fabrication and parameter control, which may be challenging to reproduce at scale.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
